## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Appamaññāvibhaṅga* is the thirteenth chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 2007]. Like the other treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*, it is structured around formal analytical sections, opening with a Sutta-oriented exposition (*suttantabhājaniya*) [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 2007]. The chapter analyzes the four "unbounded states" (*appamaññā*), which are identical with the four divine or sublime abodes (*brahmavihāra*): loving-kindness (*mettā*), compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekkhā*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].

 In automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus, the text shares extensive material across 182 canonical Pali works (totaling over 7,000 matches), most prominently with neighboring treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*—notably the *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12), *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11), *Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 10), and *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 8)—as well as the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and sections of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4, AN 9) and *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 42, SN 46) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus align the text with the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* (with a top score of 95), alongside matches in the Chinese *Dīrgha-āgama* (T 1) and *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26), the Sanskrit *Dharmasaṃgraha* and *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, and various Tibetan and Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā* texts [DharmaNexus].
